_comment: Example PrusaTray configuration with secure credential storage
_password_key_notes: password_key is a reference name for the credential
Choose a descriptive name like 'prusalink:mk4-office' or 'octoprint:garage'
On first startup, you'll be prompted to enter the password
Password is stored securely in Windows Credential Manager
Never put the actual password in this config file!

_notes: Buddy firmware (MK4/MK3.9/XL/MINI) and PrusaLink 0.8+ speak API v1.
PrusaLink 0.7.x has no /api/v1; the adapter falls back to /api/job.
Username and password are the PrusaLink credentials shown on the
printer under Settings > Network > PrusaLink (default user 'maker').
auth_mode 'digest' answers the printer's Digest challenge and also
sends the password as X-Api-Key, which Buddy firmware accepts.
auth_mode 'apikey' sends only X-Api-Key - use it if you have an API

prusaconnect._description: Prusa Connect cloud, via the Connect mobile API gateway
_notes: Host is fixed at https://connect-mobile-api.prusa3d.com; there is no
printer_base_url to set (set one only to point at a different gateway).
Prusa publishes no way to mint a token, so you supply one by hand:
sign in at connect.prusa3d.com, open the browser devtools Network tab,
and copy the Authorization header value from any /api/v1 request.
Tokens expire - if the tray goes offline with an auth error, repeat this.
printer_uuid is the printer's uuid from GET /api/v1/printers (it is also
in the connect.prusa3d.com URL when you open the printer's page).
This backend polls two endpoints per cycle (printer detail and jobs),
so consider a longer poll_interval_s (10s or more) for a cloud service.
